releaseNotes: Platform release: two people editing one thing no longer ends in silence. Whoever saved second used to overwrite the first, whose work survived only in a version history they had no reason to open — which is a strange definition of kept. A save may now name the version or timestamp it was built from, and one built from something somebody else has already replaced is refused, naming who moved it and when. "Someone changed this" is not a sentence anyone can act on, so records carry who last changed them.

Two decisions shape it. The guard is opt-in: a request that names what it read is checked, one that names nothing proceeds, because a caller who did not read the record first is not claiming to have — every existing integration keeps working, and the deliverable editor, where a person spends minutes on a change, is the place that opts in. And a refusal keeps the founder's unsaved text on the page, offering two real choices: read what the other person wrote, or save theirs as the next version anyway. Refusing without preserving the draft would be worse than the silent overwrite it replaces, because it would move the loss rather than remove it. A refused save appends no version, writes no activity, and leaves no half-written section. Checks, 214 domain tests, the production build, and the full audit pass.
